// why: The whole point of this config is signal-to-noise: a raw en_US pass over
this repo's prose reports ~160 unknown words, and roughly 85% of them are
unparty jargon (theunpartybudget, unppp, ...). The jargon collapses into
three ignoreRegExp patterns below, which leaves the genuine typos visible
instead of buried. Everything else that is a real word we just happen to
use lives in .cspell-words.txt - add to that file (or run
`./spellcheck add <word>`) rather than loosening the patterns.

dictionaryDefinitions.name: unparty
dictionaryDefinitions.description: Project vocabulary: brand terms, people, and tools we write about.

patterns.// why: cuids/hashes in generated reports (docs/reports/what-does-unparty-store.md) get split into dozens of fake 'words'. Requiring a digit keeps real long words like 'internationalization' checkable.
patterns.name: opaque-id

patterns.// why: No \b anchor: the jargon shows up mid-token too (isUnparty, aboutUNPARTY, user_unppp_visits). The suffix deliberately stops at a hyphen so a typo in `unparty-somehting` stays visible.
patterns.name: unparty-jargon
